visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged Asian man with short black hair and glasses, wearing a dark green button-down shirt, stands in front of a macro background showing bright orange salmon roe (ikura). He speaks enthusiastically, gesturing with both hands while holding a small black remote control. (2) A close-up shot replaces the man, showing a person's mouth and white teeth. A white plastic dental floss stick is being used to clean between the upper incisors. The lighting is bright and clinical. (3) A scientific diagram appears on a white background, illustrating a mouse's mouth and immune system cells like T-cells and B-cells. The man's face appears in a small circular inset at the bottom, continuing his explanation. (4) A grid of nine microscopic images shows various stages of a flossing procedure in vivo, with colorful markers indicating antigen deposition. The man is visible from the chest up against the roe background, pointing towards the screen. (5) A series of comparative photos shows human teeth before and after flossing with a fluorescent agent, highlighting the deposition efficiency between the teeth. The man continues speaking with an animated facial expression and active hand gestures.

(5) [Subtitle]: 這項發表在自然生物醫學工程上的研究. (6) [Subtitle]: 來自美國德州理工大學的團隊. (7) [Subtitle]: 我們知道多數病毒是從口鼻等黏膜入侵. (8) [Subtitle]: 但傳統打疫苗主要是在血液中產生抗體. (9) [Subtitle]: 在黏膜第一線的防禦力反而有限.
